instruction_text:
The proposal may also include "answer_requirements": an object
declaring typed evidence the answer requires to be considered
sufficient — only requirements the user message itself states or
clearly implies: {"min_items": <integer|null>, "ordering":
"newest_first"|"oldest_first"|null, "complete_coverage":
<boolean>, "ordering_semantic": <object|null>}. "min_items" is
the exact quantity the user asked for (e.g. "tres exemplos" ->
3); "ordering" applies when the user demands a superlative
position (e.g. "o ultimo", "mais recente" -> "newest_first");
"complete_coverage" is true only when the user asks for ALL
items or an authoritative total.
When "ordering" is set AND the demand refers to a business event
the ordering expresses (e.g. "o ultimo alterado"), you may add
"ordering_semantic": {"event": "modification", "field":
"<a field present in the returned records>", "contract_evidence":
"<a verbatim quote from the selected capability description
stating that field's meaning>"}. "ordering_semantic" only
interprets the RETURNED records — it is never a request argument
and adds no filters. Quote only text that literally appears in
the capability description; never invent a field or a meaning.
Omit "ordering_semantic" when no declared field meaning
supports the claim. Use nulls or omit the object when the
request is a plain read with no stated quantity, ordering or
coverage demand.
